texts.li: Last night's card game went late, and by the end {B_nameDef} had bet {B_possessive} good coat on a pair of twos and lost. {A_nameDef} has worn it every day since and keeps mentioning how warm it is.\n\n{B_nameDef} says the deck was marked. {A_nameDef} says {B_nameDef} can't count. Both want the council to rule on it.

{A_nameDef} won a week of {B_nameDef}'s dinners at dice, fairly and in front of witnesses. Three days in, {B_nameDef} is living on scraps and has started eyeing {A_nameDef}'s plate.\n\n"A bet is a bet," says {A_nameDef}. The others would like the council to step in before someone gets a fork in the hand.

li.label: Make {B_nameDef} pay up
li.outcome: The debt stands. {A_nameDef} is enjoying the winnings, and {B_nameDef} is paying up with bad grace.
li.riskOutcome: The debt stands. {B_nameDef} wouldn't hear of it, and the argument came to blows.

li.label: Call the bet off
li.outcome: The bet is off. {A_nameDef} handed back the winnings one coin at a time, and has been sour about it since.

li.label: Ban gambling in the colony
li.outcome: The council banned gambling and canceled every debt. The cards went into the fire; the dice have not turned up.

li.label: Double or nothing
li.outcome: They played one more hand with the council watching. {A_nameDef} won again. {B_nameDef} now owes twice as much and has gone off alone to brood about it.
li.riskOutcome: They played one more hand with the council watching, and {B_nameDef} won everything back. {A_nameDef} took the loss badly, and the onlookers enjoyed every minute of it.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} went into {A_nameDef}'s room looking for a borrowed hammer and found a hoard under the bed: the good knives, the softest blanket in the colony, a dozen missing spoons, and {COUNT} {THING} that should have been in the stores.\n\n{A_nameDef} calls it a collection. {B_nameDef} calls it theft.

For weeks small things have been going missing around the colony, a spoon, a shirt, the good chair from the dining room. {B_nameDef} finally followed the scuff marks to {A_nameDef}'s room and found all of it neatly arranged, with {COUNT} {THING} tucked under the mattress.\n\n{A_nameDef} says {A_pronoun} was only keeping it safe. {B_nameDef} wants it back in the stores by supper.

li.label: Confiscate the lot
li.outcome: The hoard went back into the stockpiles, {THING} and all. {A_nameDef} is sulking in {A_possessive} emptied room.
li.riskOutcome: The hoard went back into the stockpiles. {A_nameDef} took it badly and started smashing furniture.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} keep it
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} keeps the collection. {B_nameDef} has started hiding {B_possessive} own things and says the council has rewarded a thief.

li.label: Return half to the stores
li.outcome: Half the hoard went back to the stores. {A_nameDef} got to choose which half, and some of the others think {A_pronoun} kept the better part.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} woke the colony last night screaming about fire. In the dream the fields were burning, the sky was burning, and people stood in the smoke without faces. {A_nameDef} has described it at every meal since.\n\nSome of the others have started watching the horizon.

Three nights running, {A_nameDef} has dreamed of smoke over the walls, a red sky, and a voice counting backward from ten. {A_nameDef} is certain it's a warning.\n\nA few others are starting to believe it, and the night watch has grown jumpy.

li.label: Double the watch
li.outcome: The council doubled the watch. {A_nameDef} is glad to be taken seriously, but between the extra shifts and the talk of fire, the others are sleeping badly.

li.label: Laugh it off at dinner
li.outcome: The council made a joke of it at dinner and the table laughed along. {A_nameDef} didn't laugh, and has stopped talking about the dreams.
li.riskOutcome: The council made a joke of it at dinner. {A_nameDef} left halfway through, walked out past the fields, and hasn't come back yet.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} hold a ceremony
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} had each colonist mark a fear on a scrap of wood and throw it on a bonfire. Some felt foolish doing it, but people slept better afterward.

li.label: Tell {A_nameDef} to keep it quiet
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} has been told to stop describing the dreams at meals. The dreams still come most nights, and the talk of them hasn't died down.

texts.li: Years ago, long before this colony, a band from {FACTION} found {A_nameDef} half-dead in a ditch and nursed {A_objective} back to health without asking for a thing. Word has come that they've had a hard season.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to send them silver. It's the colony's silver, so it's the council's call.

{A_nameDef} rarely talks about life before the colony. Last night, after a beer, {A_nameDef} told how {FACTION} once took {A_objective} in when no one else would, and how {A_pronoun} left one morning without a word of thanks.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants to make it right with a gift of the colony's silver, and is asking the council for it.

li.label: Send them 100 silver
li.outcome: A hundred silver went to {FACTION} with a short letter from {A_nameDef}, and they sent back warm thanks. Not everyone thinks it was money well spent.
li.riskOutcome: The silver went out with a passing caravan and never reached {FACTION}. The caravan hasn't been seen since.

li.label: Send 25 silver as a token
li.outcome: {FACTION} got 25 silver and a polite note from {A_nameDef}, who had hoped to send more.

li.label: Send them food instead
li.outcome: A load of food went to {FACTION}, who needed it more than silver. The storeroom is noticeably emptier.

li.label: We need it more than they do
li.outcome: The silver stays in the colony. {A_nameDef} didn't argue, but has barely spoken to anyone since.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} knocked a shelf while cleaning, and {A_nameDef}'s carved wooden bird fell and broke in four pieces. It was the only thing {A_nameDef} still had from home.\n\n{B_nameDef} keeps saying it was an accident, more often than seems necessary. {A_nameDef} wants the council to do something about it.

{A_nameDef} carried an old pocket watch that hadn't worked in years. {B_nameDef} borrowed it to fix it, as a surprise, and handed it back in a cupped palm.\n\n{A_nameDef} is grieving over a handful of springs. {B_nameDef} is very sorry and would like that to be the end of it.

li.label: {B_nameDef} apologizes publicly
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} apologized at dinner, with the others listening. It was stiff, but {A_nameDef} accepted it.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} apologized at dinner through clenched teeth, and it was plain {B_pronoun} didn't mean a word of it.

li.label: Pay {A_nameDef} 50 silver
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} received fifty silver from the colony for the loss. It won't mend anything, but {A_nameDef} appreciated the gesture.

li.label: Have {B_nameDef} make a new one
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} spent three evenings making a replacement. It isn't the same, but {A_nameDef} keeps it on the shelf where the old one was.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} spent three evenings on a replacement, but it came out crude and lopsided, nothing like the original.

li.label: Call it an accident
li.outcome: The council called it an accident. {A_nameDef} has kept the pieces in a pouch and no longer trusts {B_nameDef} around {A_possessive} things.

texts.li: With raiders seen in the hills, {B_nameDef} had the night watch. {A_nameDef} came out in the small hours and found {B_nameDef} curled up against the wall, asleep, {B_possessive} weapon lying in the dirt.\n\n{A_nameDef} wants it dealt with before nightfall.

{A_nameDef} came to the council at dawn, white with anger. {B_nameDef} slept through the whole watch last night while some large animal snuffled and scratched at the gate.\n\nIt didn't get in. {A_nameDef} wants to know what happens next time.

li.label: Punish {B_nameDef} with extra shifts
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is hauling and digging from dawn to dusk until the council says otherwise. Most of the colony thinks it was deserved.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} took the punishment, then took a swing at {A_nameDef} for reporting it.

li.label: Warn {B_nameDef} privately
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} got a private warning and swore it won't happen again. {A_nameDef} has started checking on the watch at night anyway.
li.riskOutcome: The council spoke to {B_nameDef} in private. Two nights later {B_nameDef} was found asleep on watch again, and this time word got around.

li.label: Put {A_nameDef} in charge of the watch
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} now runs the night watch, with a strict schedule, a whistle and surprise checks. {B_nameDef}'s name comes up on the schedule often.

li.label: Let it go this time
li.outcome: The matter was dropped. {A_nameDef} has stopped sleeping well, and keeps getting up to check the gate.
li.riskOutcome: The council let it go, but {A_nameDef} wouldn't. The next argument with {B_nameDef} ended in a fight.

texts.li: {A_nameDef}'s new sculpture stands next to the dining table, and it is clearly {B_nameDef}, down to the squint, with a nose half again the size of the real one.\n\n{B_nameDef} has started eating outside and wants the thing gone. {A_nameDef} says it's an honest likeness.

{A_nameDef} calls the new piece "Study of a Colonist, Mid-Excuse." The others recognized {B_nameDef} in it straight away, and laughed.\n\n{B_nameDef} has asked the council, very calmly, to have it removed before {B_nameDef} takes a hammer to it.

li.label: Smash it
li.outcome: The council had the sculpture smashed. {B_nameDef} swept up the pieces, smiling, while {A_nameDef} watched from the doorway.
li.riskOutcome: The council had the sculpture smashed. {A_nameDef} couldn't bear it and walked off, dazed, before the sweeping was done.

li.label: Keep it on display
li.outcome: The sculpture stays. Visitors like it, and the colony still laughs at it. {B_nameDef} eats with {B_possessive} back to it.
li.riskOutcome: The sculpture stays. A few days later {B_nameDef} snapped over breakfast and went after the sculptor.

li.label: Make {A_nameDef} carve an apology piece
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} carved a second {B_nameDef}, this one square-jawed and gazing nobly into the distance. {B_nameDef} grumbled about it, but accepted the apology.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} carved an apology piece. It is flattering, apart from the dunce cap on its head, and it has made things worse.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has built a homemade fiddle and practices on it every night after the others have gone to bed. {B_nameDef} sleeps on the other side of the wall and hasn't had a full night's sleep in four days.\n\n{B_nameDef} came to the council red-eyed, still holding {B_possessive} pillow.

Every night, just as the colony settles down, the drumming starts. {A_nameDef} says it helps {A_objective} think.\n\n{B_nameDef} hasn't slept properly in a week, and has asked the council, politely for now, to make it stop.

li.label: Ban the night music
li.outcome: The night music is banned. {B_nameDef} slept fourteen hours straight. {A_nameDef} is sulking, and drums on the table at every meal.

li.label: Set quiet hours after midnight
li.outcome: Music until midnight, silence after. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} both grumble about the arrangement, but it's holding.
li.riskOutcome: Quiet hours were agreed, but {A_nameDef} keeps playing past midnight, and {B_nameDef} is lying awake again.

li.label: Tell {B_nameDef} to live with it
li.outcome: The music plays on, and {A_nameDef} is slowly getting better at it. {B_nameDef} sleeps with rags stuffed in both ears and is worn out most days.
li.riskOutcome: The music plays on. Two nights later {B_nameDef} snapped and started breaking things.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} have agreed to settle their quarrel with a fight. Fists only, at dawn, behind the stockpile, with anyone who wants to watch.\n\nThey want the council's blessing, mostly so the loser can't complain afterward.

{B_nameDef} threw a glove at {A_nameDef}'s feet this morning. It was a dirty work glove, and {A_nameDef} took that as part of the insult.\n\nThey want to settle it properly, in the yard, with witnesses, and are asking the council's permission.

li.label: Allow the duel
li.outcome: The duel was held at dawn with a crowd cheering. It ended with blood, a loose tooth, and a handshake that both of them meant.

li.label: Forbid it
li.outcome: There will be no duel. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} still glare at each other across every room they share.
li.riskOutcome: The council forbade the duel. {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} held it anyway, behind the latrine, with no witnesses and no rules.

li.label: Make them shake hands in public
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} shook hands at the evening meal, in front of the others. Both squeezed hard and neither smiled, but it's done.
li.riskOutcome: The handshake turned into a shoving match, and then into a proper fight, while the onlookers cheered.

li.label: Settle it with a hauling race
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} spent the afternoon racing each other to haul stone. A lot of work got done, and they've been on better terms since.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} raced each other hauling stone. The loser accused the winner of cheating, and it came to blows.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has opinions about how the colony is run and wants them to count. {A_nameDef} is asking for a formal seat on the council, with a vote, a chair at the head of the table, and a title.\n\n{A_nameDef} has suggested several titles. Most of them begin with "High."

{A_nameDef} pinned a list of demands to the dining room door overnight. Item one is a seat on the council. Items two through eleven assume item one.\n\nPeople are reading it over breakfast, and some of them are nodding.

li.label: Grant {A_nameDef} a title
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} was given the title of Warden, of nothing in particular. {A_nameDef} is delighted with it, and a few of the others are jealous.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} was named Warden and is taking it very seriously. Several people have already been told off for sitting in the wrong chair.

li.label: Refuse the request
li.outcome: The request was refused. {A_nameDef} said nothing at the meeting and has been in a foul mood ever since.

li.label: Put {A_nameDef} in charge of the storeroom
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is now in charge of the storeroom and has already relabeled every shelf in it.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} asked for a seat at the table and was given the storeroom keys instead, and took it as an insult.

li.label: Let {A_nameDef} sit in on one meeting
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} sat through four hours of debate about where to dig the new latrine and has withdrawn the request.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} sat through four hours of debate about the latrine and enjoyed all of it. {A_nameDef} now comes to every meeting, invited or not.

texts.li: {A_nameDef} has been keeping a tally of work hours on the workshop wall, one column for {A_nameDef} and one for {B_nameDef}. {B_nameDef}'s column is mostly empty.\n\n{A_nameDef} has started underlining things and wants the council to come and look.

{A_nameDef} came to the council with dirt up to the elbows and pointed out the window at {B_nameDef}, who was lying in the grass at noon, watching clouds. "Every day," {A_nameDef} said.\n\n{B_nameDef} says it's called thinking. {A_nameDef} says it's called lying down.

li.label: Side with {A_nameDef}: double shifts for {B_nameDef}
li.outcome: {B_nameDef} is on double shifts until the tally evens out, and {A_nameDef} keeps the count on the wall up to date.
li.riskOutcome: {B_nameDef} is on double shifts, and opened the first one by throwing a shovel at {A_nameDef}.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} keep {B_possessive} own pace
li.outcome: The council ruled that people work at different speeds. {B_nameDef} went back to {B_possessive} usual pace, and {A_nameDef} took the ruling badly.

li.label: Pair them up on every shift
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work every shift together. {B_nameDef} is picking up the pace, mostly to make the lecturing stop.
li.riskOutcome: {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} now work every shift together, and {A_nameDef} ends up doing most of {B_nameDef}'s share.

li.label: Stay out of it
li.outcome: The council stayed out of it. The tally on the workshop wall keeps getting longer.
li.riskOutcome: The council stayed out of it, and {A_nameDef} has eased off too. {A_nameDef} sees no reason to work harder than anyone else.

texts.li: {B_nameDef} swears that {A_nameDef} rode with the raiders who burned {B_possessive} home, years ago and far from here. {A_nameDef} hasn't denied it, and hasn't said anything else either.\n\nThe others are starting to take sides, and the council needs to speak first.

It came out over dinner. {A_nameDef} was telling the story behind an old scar and named the place where {A_pronoun} got it, and {B_nameDef} was on {B_possessive} feet with a knife in hand. {B_nameDef} says {A_nameDef} helped burn that place to the ground.\n\n{A_nameDef} says it was a long time ago, with different people, and that {A_pronoun} was someone else then. The council has to decide whether that's enough.

li.label: The past is past
li.outcome: The council ruled that what {A_nameDef} did before the colony stays in the past. {B_nameDef} left the table and hasn't eaten with the others since.
li.riskOutcome: The council ruled that the past is past. {B_nameDef} walked out of the meeting and kept walking.

li.label: {A_nameDef} earns {A_possessive} place
li.outcome: {A_nameDef} is working the hardest jobs in the colony, without complaint, until the council is satisfied. {B_nameDef} watches every shift.

li.label: Let {B_nameDef} have one swing
li.outcome: The council looked away for one minute. {B_nameDef} used all of it, and {A_nameDef} didn't raise a hand until the very end.

li.label: Keep it between them
li.outcome: The council told {A_nameDef} and {B_nameDef} to keep it to themselves. {B_nameDef} agreed, and hasn't turned {B_possessive} back on {A_nameDef} since.
li.riskOutcome: The council tried to keep it quiet, but by morning the story was out. {A_nameDef} has been eating alone since.
